phase3_findings.description: _CatalogView does not enforce that every kept field is in fields; a misspelled kept name silently drops out of the projection.
_CATALOG_VIEWS is a mutable module-level dict although it decides which catalog fields are exposed under every rule set.
_rewalk's expected cache is keyed only by view name; reuse across rule sets would compare against another set's filter (no current path does this).
Live test that an error-raising condition never runs on a hidden row covers only TABLES, not COLUMNS or KEY_COLUMN_USAGE.
No unit test places a catalog view in a nested scope (EXISTS subquery or CTE body) to confirm it is rewritten.
test_key_column_usage_lists_only_keys_inside_the_set calls pytest.skip after its main assertions pass when SQLLENS_TEST_MYSQL_OTHER_DATABASE is unset, reporting a partly verified run as skipped.
docs/external/rule-sets.md 'Common reasons' bullet is ambiguous about which clause 'other than the three schema-lookup views' qualifies.
Two added test comments in test_system_prompt.py record where pinned text came from rather than what a change would break.

report:
## Verdict: APPROVE with notes (eight Suggestion findings and two inconclusive checklist items; no failures)

The PR is ready to merge: no reviewer raised anything at Important or above, every checklist item that could be settled passed, and the two inconclusive items only lacked access to the sqlglot library source.

Rule applied: rule 6 — findings below the threshold and INCONCLUSIVE items remain → APPROVE with notes

## Code Review Findings

### 🟡 Suggestion / Minor (8)

<details><summary>8 items</summary>

1. `src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py` lines 92-97: `_CatalogView` does not check that every `kept` field is in `fields`; a misspelled kept name would silently drop out of the projection. (raised by 1/6 agents)
2. `src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py` lines 103-141: `_CATALOG_VIEWS` is a plain mutable `dict`, although it decides which catalog fields are exposed under every rule set; a read-only mapping would enforce that. (raised by 1/6 agents)
3. `src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py` lines 468-476: the `expected` cache passed to `_rewalk` is keyed only by view name, so reusing one dict across two rule sets would compare against the wrong filter; today each statement gets a fresh dict. (raised by 1/6 agents)
4. `tests/connectors/test_rule_sets_mysql.py` lines 597-608: the live test that an error-raising condition never runs on a hidden row covers only `TABLES`, not `COLUMNS` or `KEY_COLUMN_USAGE`. (raised by 1/6 agents)
5. `tests/unit/test_safety_rule_sets.py` around lines 460-465: no unit test puts a catalog view inside a nested scope (an `EXISTS` subquery or a CTE body) to confirm it is rewritten. (raised by 1/6 agents)
6. `tests/connectors/test_rule_sets_mysql.py` lines 589-594: `test_key_column_usage_lists_only_keys_inside_the_set` calls `pytest.skip` after its main assertions pass when `SQLLENS_TEST_MYSQL_OTHER_DATABASE` is unset, so a run that checked the in-set rows reports as skipped. (raised by 1/6 agents)
7. `docs/external/rule-sets.md` line 115: the "Common reasons" bullet does not make clear which clause "other than the three schema-lookup views" qualifies. (raised by 1/6 agents)
8. `tests/unit/test_system_prompt.py`: two added comments record where the pinned text came from rather than what a change would break (location not confirmed). (raised by 1/6 agents)

</details>

- VC-2: INCONCLUSIVE (important) — exp.CurrentSchema() generates MySQL SCHEMA(), equivalent to DATABASE(), so the filter keeps only rows of the connected database. [src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  rule_sets.py:326-327 builds _in_schema as CAST(field AS BINARY) = CAST(exp.CurrentSchema() AS BINARY), so the filter does rest on sqlglot's MySQL rendering of exp.CurrentSchema. The item supplies no dependency_sources and the views hold no vendored sqlglot, so I could not read the sqlglot MySQL generator under an approved directory. tests/unit/test_safety_rule_sets.py:322-351 expects 'SCHEMA()' output, but that is the PR's own test text and not library source. Missing evidence: sqlglot/dialects/mysql.py and generator handling of CurrentSchema (not run or read). I did not run MySQL, so I did not confirm SCHEMA() equals DATABASE() semantics either.

  </details>

- VC-3: INCONCLUSIVE (suggestion) — _binary builds CAST(x AS BINARY) via exp.DataType.build('BINARY', dialect='mysql'), giving byte-for-byte comparison of catalog names against the literal lists in MySQL, matching the existing catalog existence check. [src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  Repo side verified: safety/rule_sets.py:321-323 _binary returns exp.Cast(this=node, to=exp.DataType.build('BINARY', dialect=_DIALECT)) with _DIALECT='mysql' (line 71). The existence check in src/sqllens/rule_sets.py:443-514 compares names in Python with exact string equality (kinds.get(table.name), 'column in present'), documented as 'byte for byte' (line 449), so a binary comparison in SQL is consistent with it. Unit tests (tests/unit/test_safety_rule_sets.py:322-340) expect rendered SQL 'CAST(`TABLE_NAME` AS BINARY)'. Not settled: no dependency_sources were supplied and no sqlglot expressions.py was found (Glob of site-packages/sqlglot under the repo returned nothing), so I could not read sqlglot DataType.build for 'BINARY' under mysql, and I did not run the tests. Missing evidence: sqlglot source (DataType.build / mysql generator for DataType.Type.BINARY) or a test run confirming the rendering.

  </details>

- <details><summary>✅ Passed items (27 of 29)</summary>

  - VC-1: _CATALOG_VIEWS lists every field of MySQL 8.0+ information_schema.TABLES (21), COLUMNS (22) and KEY_COLUMN_USAGE (12) in the view's own order, so SELECT * over the rewritten derived table yields the same field list as the real view. [src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py]
  - VC-4: A derived table ending in LIMIT 18446744073709551615 is materialized by MySQL and not merged or condition-pushed, so a model WHERE expression (e.g. IF(TABLE_NAME='salaries', EXP(1000), 0)) never evaluates on a filtered-out catalog row. [src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py]
  - VC-5: Removing the LIMIT is the only thing standing between the model's conditions and hidden catalog rows; with it, MySQL neither merges nor pushes conditions into the derived table, and 18446744073709551615 is the largest value MySQL's LIMIT takes. [src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py]
  - VC-6: The KEY_COLUMN_USAGE filter keeps a row only when its table/column pair is listed in DATABASE() and either all three REFERENCED_* fields are NULL or the referenced schema is DATABASE() and the referenced table/column pair is listed; a foreign key into another database or an unlisted table is hidden. [src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py]
  - VC-7: _catalog_filter builds IN lists from the mapping; an empty tables mapping or a table with no listed columns yields an IN with an empty list, which sqlglot/MySQL must handle (generate valid SQL or refuse) rather than error unguarded. [src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py]
  - VC-8: _catalog_view recognizes information_schema.<TABLES|COLUMNS|KEY_COLUMN_USAGE> in any letter case only when db is an Identifier and catalog is absent; a catalog-qualified reference (def.information_schema.tables) falls to _check_reference and is refused as KIND_CATALOG. [src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py]
  - VC-9: _is_catalog_derived accepts a catalog table only when its parent is the From of a Select that is the this of a Subquery with only this/alias/joins args and no column aliases, and the body generates text identical to _catalog_body for the view and the same tables; any reference elsewhere raises KIND_UNCHECKED in _rewalk. [src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py]
  - VC-10: A catalog view joined via a JOIN inside the guard's derived wrapper (wrapper joins arg, or a joined table in the body) cannot pass: the body text comparison and the From-parent check reject a catalog Table that sits in a Join rather than the body's From. [src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py]
  - VC-11: The expected-text cache passed to both _rewalk calls in apply_rule_set is built from the same tables mapping, and the monkeypatched _rewalk in the unit test matches the new (tree, tables, expected=None) signature. [src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py]
  - VC-12: _analyze's second return value changed to a tuple (base, catalog); every caller of _analyze is updated to unpack it. [src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py]
  - VC-13: _wrap keeps the original alias or, without one, the table name as written (e.g. `tables`, `TABLES`, `Tables`), so the model's column qualifiers like TABLES.TABLE_NAME still resolve against the derived table. [src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py]
  - VC-14: The internal doc asserts a model expression never runs on a hidden row, and that the re-walk accepts a catalog view only inside a derived table whose body generates the same MySQL text as _catalog_body builds. [docs/internal/database-connectors/rule-sets.md]
  - VC-15: The changelog and external doc state other catalog views, the mysql, performance_schema and sys schemas, and SHOW statements are still refused, and every field other than names, types and key details comes back NULL. [changelog.d/393.added.md]
  - VC-16: The external rule-sets doc refusal bullet says a query naming a schema or catalog other than the three lookup views, or running SHOW, is refused, and the three views show only the selected set's tables, listed columns and keys among them in the connected database. [docs/external/rule-sets.md]
  - VC-17: With rule_sets=False the introspection sentence is byte-identical to the pre-change prompt (same text and f-string interpolation of catalog_example), and with rule_sets=True only that sentence changes beyond the two #374 lines. [src/sqllens/agent/core/system_prompt/default.py]
  - VC-18: The rule-set introspection sentence is used whenever rule_sets is True regardless of dialect, including when no dialect resolves, unlike the qualify-column rule which needs a dialect. [src/sqllens/agent/core/system_prompt/default.py]
  - VC-19: CI creates database sqllens_other and grants the test user 'sqllens'@'%' ALL on it, and passes SQLLENS_TEST_MYSQL_OTHER_DATABASE=sqllens_other to the connector test step; the test user name matches the CI MySQL service user. [.github/workflows/ci.yml]
  - VC-20: The connector fixture creates rs_customers with a FOREIGN KEY to rs_salaries before rs_salaries exists, relying on FOREIGN_KEY_CHECKS=0 set in _TEARDOWN persisting on the same connection; teardown drops tables with checks off on its own new connection. [tests/connectors/test_rule_sets_mysql.py]
  - VC-21: test_key_column_usage_lists_only_keys_inside_the_set asserts the unguarded view row tuple (other, 'rs_orders', 'id', None, None) and (schema,'rs_orders','customer_id',other,'rs_customers'), but the unguarded query filters TABLE_NAME LIKE 'rs\_%' without a schema filter, so these rows depend on the other database's tables being visible to the test user. [tests/connectors/test_rule_sets_mysql.py]
  - VC-22: Under the example set, `SELECT TABLE_NAME FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TABLES WHERE TABLE_SCHEMA = DATABASE()` returns exactly `customers` and `orders`, and the same query written as `select table_name from information_schema.tables where table_schema = database()` returns the same rows. [src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py:227-238,340-403]
  - VC-23: Under the example set, `INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS` returns exactly the five listed columns, with no row for `email`, `discount` or `rep_id`. [src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py:340-391]
  - VC-24: Under the example set, `INFORMATION_SCHEMA.KEY_COLUMN_USAGE` returns the primary-key rows for `customers.id` and `orders.id` and the foreign-key row from `orders.customer_id` to `customers.id`, and it returns no row whose table, column, referenced table or referenced column is outside the set, and no row whose schema or referenced schema is another database (a same-named `orders` table in another database the SQL Lens user can read included). [src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py]
  - VC-25: Under the example set, `SELECT TABLE_NAME FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TABLES WHERE IF(TABLE_NAME = 'salaries', EXP(1000), 0) > 0` returns no row and raises no error. [src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py]
  - VC-26: Under the example set, a catalog read of a field outside the 25 kept fields (for example `TABLE_ROWS`, `COLUMN_DEFAULT` or `CONSTRAINT_NAME`) returns `NULL` for it, and `SELECT *` over a rewritten view returns every field of that view, each field outside the kept fields `NULL`. [src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py]
  - VC-27: A rewritten statement in which a reference to `INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TABLES`, `COLUMNS` or `KEY_COLUMN_USAGE` sits outside the catalog derived table the guard builds for it is refused (a planted defect in a unit test), and a read of `INFORMATION_SCHEMA.STATISTICS` or `SHOW TABLES` is still refused. [tests/unit/test_safety_rule_sets.py]
  - VC-28: While a rule-set file is configured, the system prompt's MySQL schema-lookup guidance names `INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TABLES`, `COLUMNS` and `KEY_COLUMN_USAGE` and permits no `SHOW` statement, and the prompt differs from #374's rule-set prompt for the same configuration by that change only. [src/sqllens/agent/core/system_prompt/default.py]
  - VC-29: Without a rule-set file configured, catalog reads return what they return today, and the system prompt is byte-identical to today's for the same configuration. [src/sqllens/agent/core/system_prompt/default.py]

  </details>
- Reviewed against issue #379 — criteria from the workpad; scope unchanged.

</details>
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Under the example set, `SELECT TABLE_NAME FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TABLES WHERE TABLE_SCHEMA = DATABASE()` returns exactly `customers` and `orders`, and the same query written as `select table_name from information_schema.tables where table_schema = database()` returns the same rows.
- [ ] Under the example set, `INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS` returns exactly the five listed columns, with no row for `email`, `discount` or `rep_id`.
- [ ] Under the example set, `INFORMATION_SCHEMA.KEY_COLUMN_USAGE` returns the primary-key rows for `customers.id` and `orders.id` and the foreign-key row from `orders.customer_id` to `customers.id`, and it returns no row whose table, column, referenced table or referenced column is outside the set, and no row whose schema or referenced schema is another database (a same-named `orders` table in another database the SQL Lens user can read included).
- [ ] Under the example set, `SELECT TABLE_NAME FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TABLES WHERE IF(TABLE_NAME = 'salaries', EXP(1000), 0) > 0` returns no row and raises no error.
- [ ] Under the example set, a catalog read of a field outside the 25 kept fields (for example `TABLE_ROWS`, `COLUMN_DEFAULT` or `CONSTRAINT_NAME`) returns `NULL` for it, and `SELECT *` over a rewritten view returns every field of that view, each field outside the kept fields `NULL`.
- [ ] A rewritten statement in which a reference to `INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TABLES`, `COLUMNS` or `KEY_COLUMN_USAGE` sits outside the catalog derived table the guard builds for it is refused (a planted defect in a unit test), and a read of `INFORMATION_SCHEMA.STATISTICS` or `SHOW TABLES` is still refused.
- [ ] While a rule-set file is configured, the system prompt's MySQL schema-lookup guidance names `INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TABLES`, `COLUMNS` and `KEY_COLUMN_USAGE` and permits no `SHOW` statement, and the prompt differs from #374's rule-set prompt for the same configuration by that change only.
- [ ] Without a rule-set file configured, catalog reads return what they return today, and the system prompt is byte-identical to today's for the same configuration.
